purpose: Fostamatinib is used to treat a condition called chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in adults. ITP is when your immune system mistakenly destroys your platelets, which are the tiny blood cells that help your blood clot. This medicine helps raise your platelet count to reduce your risk of bleeding.
how_it_works: Your immune system has certain cells that attack and destroy your platelets by mistake. Fostamatinib works by blocking a specific protein in those immune cells called SYK, which acts like an 'on switch' for the attack. By turning off that switch, fewer platelets get destroyed and your platelet count goes back up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include high blood pressure, diarrhea, nausea, dizziness, and increased liver enzyme levels in your blood. You may also notice stomach pain, tiredness, chest pain, or a rash. Let your doctor know if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medication can cause high blood pressure, so your blood pressure will need to be checked regularly. It can also raise your liver enzyme levels, which means your liver will need to be monitored with blood tests. Fostamatinib can harm an unborn baby, so women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one month after stopping. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as fostamatinib can interact with many common drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg taken by mouth twice a day with or without food. If your platelet count does not respond well enough after about 4 weeks, your doctor may increase the dose to 150 mg twice a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
